title: DPO vs SFT dual sparsity and cross-task interference in a linear softmax policy
setting: A linear softmax policy over K=4 candidate responses per prompt with sparse binary features (d=128). Task A pairs are labeled by a noisy hidden linear reward. Each policy is trained from a random reference by full-batch GD for 300 steps, with the learning rate chosen from a shared 9-value grid on a validation set of fresh task-A prompts. Interference is the increase in NLL of preferred responses on fresh task-B samples, whose feature coordinates partly overlap with task A. A third arm trains DPO on randomly flipped labels as a null.

paper.title: On the Sparsity of Direct Preference Optimization: Weight Disentanglement in the NTK Regime
paper.claim: DPO updates are dual-sparse (concentrated on few support pairs, sparse in parameters) and so cause less cross-task interference than SFT updates.

metric.name: interference
metric.description: Mean NLL of preferred responses on fresh task-B samples after training on task A, minus the same NLL at the reference parameters (nats). Lower means less cross-task interference. Diagnostics: top10_mass (share of total per-pair coefficient mass held by the top 10% of pairs), param_sparsity (fraction of task-A coordinates with |delta| < 5% of max), heldout_reward_gain (gain in expected true reward on fresh task-A prompts), overlap_norm (norm of the update on coordinates shared with task B).

factors.name: method
factors.description: SFT on chosen responses, DPO on preference pairs, or DPO on randomly flipped labels (null).

factors.name: density
factors.description: Bernoulli density of the binary response features; dense features weaken gradient cancellation and sparsity.

factors.name: beta
factors.description: DPO temperature, which sets the logistic margin scale and how quickly pairs saturate (ignored by SFT).

factors.name: n_pairs
factors.description: Number of training preference pairs on task A.
